claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A physics-informed transformer combining microstructural descriptors, composition, and processing history can predict mechanical properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
High-resolution imaging or multiscale simulations can supply descriptors that adequately capture the alloy's multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The transformer can predict Young's modulus of HfNbTiVAl10 with an error below 10%.
The transformer can predict yield strength of HfNbTiVAl10 with an error below 10%.
The transformer will significantly improve the reliability of fracture-toughness predictions for HfNbTiVAl10.
Prior CALPHAD, first-principles, and standard machine-learning methods typically have prediction errors of 15–20% for the relevant properties.
Once pre-trained, a transformer requires fewer computational resources than DFT-based screening.
The proposed model will be at least 10 times faster than conventional CALPHAD or first-principles methods.
Transformer self-attention can expose feature importance and interactions among alloying elements.
Transformer representations can capture local interactions and long-range dependencies relevant to mechanical-property prediction.
Self-attention can identify and weight local and long-range interactions among high-resolution microstructural features.
Pre-training followed by fine-tuning on limited HEA data reduces the amount of data and the number of training epochs needed.
Pre-training and fine-tuning improve generalization and reduce overfitting on limited HEA datasets.
The cited transfer-learning results extend to elastic modulus and fracture toughness.
The model will lose reliability when the input microstructure lies outside the representational domain of its pre-training data.
Extreme temperatures, unanticipated phase transformations, or unrepresented microstructural evolution can place samples outside the model's reliable domain.
Fracture-toughness prediction reliability depends on the quality and physical representativeness of the extracted microstructural descriptors.
